newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 1.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- JCI Ltd's proposed merger with British-based Lonrho foundered, but the South African group might clinch a consolation deal in which its Tavistock coal mining company merges with Lonrho's coal producer, Duiker Mining, insiders said.

- Network Healthcare Holdings Ltd is set to take a controlling stake in private hospital group Clinic Holdings, including eight unlisted hospitals in the Clinic stable, in a deal that sources valued at between 950 million rand and one billion rand.
- The Financial Services Board is pushing for regulation of foreign-registered investment products in an attempt to protect local investors after exchange control regulations are relaxed.
- An investigation of the South African Tourism Board could result in its being closed and replaced with an efficient national marketing structure.
- Former housing director-general Billy Cobbett has been appointed by Cape Town municipality to tack one of the thorniest housing problems in any of the country's major metropolitan areas.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Tiny Rowland, the former head of British conglomerate Lonrho, said that a failed proposal to merge Lonrho and JCI showed that the company's board had acted in the interest of all shareholders.
- A breakaway labour group formed at Amplats' platinum mine at Rustenburg denied responsibility for killings that have led to labour unrest at the mine.
- Gold slipped to a four-and-a-half-year low of $334.05 an ounce on Monday as negative sentiment in the bullion market pulled it down.
- Howard Mitchell, managing director of of Epic Foods, has resigned -- just a day after Doug Band, chairman of the Premier Group, said the division was "going according to plan".
SAKE-BEELD

- The rand fell by 1.5 cents against the dollar on Monday to its lowest level in five months. The fall came on the eve of relaxation of exchange controls, but analysts said there was no reason for concern.
- Black economic empowerment groups will take a 22.5 percent share in the new company which will manage the horse racing industry in Gauteng province.
THE CITIZEN
- Biting cold is expected over the central regions of the interior following snowfalls in the Free State, KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga, the Weather Bureau said.
- President Nelson Mandela has sent congratulatory messages to Chinese President Jiang Zemin, Hong Kong's chief executive Tung Chee-Hwa and the people of Hong Kong on their reunification with China.
- The South African rand fell to a five-month low as banks stocked up on dollars ahead of a milestone relaxation of foreign exchange controls.
--Johannesburg newsroom -27-11-482.1003
